Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood PM), Daniel Park (AstraNova Head of Search), Erin Soto (AstraNova ML), Ravi Patel (AstraNova Security), Nina Gomez (Product)
Shared links: deck: https://redwood.app/slides/astanova-intro, pilot-sheet: https://sheets.redwood/pilot-astanova, perf-bench: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/2027-06-abridged

Auto-summary (auto):
- Demo of Hosted API embeddings + reranker endpoints focusing on medical records search relevance.
- Walkthrough of end-to-end flow: embed, store vectors, initial retrieval, reranker call to hosted API.
- Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, data residency, VPC options, KMS integration, and evaluation metrics (MRR/NDCG).
- Agreed next steps: pilot proposal + security package, pilot dataset upload, technical kickoff next week.

Topics (auto): embeddings pipeline, reranker API, hosted vs dedicated, VPC/private options, SOC2/KMS, evaluation metrics, performance benchmarks

---- Transcript body ----
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya with Redwood, Liam is our solutions engineer, priya product, and from AstraNova we have daniel, erin, r ravi and nina. Can you hear me ok?
[00:10] Daniel (AstraNova): Yep, we can hear you, thanks.
[00:12] Erin (AstraNova): All good here.
[00:15] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda: we'll run through the hosted API flow for embeddings and our reranker endpoint, show an example with a small med-records dataset, then talk ops and security. We'll leave time for Qs. Sound good?
[00:25] Daniel: Yup. We're most interested in better relevance for clinical note search and being able to keep PII on-prem where needed.
[00:30] Liam (Redwood): Great, I'll share screen. heads up transcription might mess up some acronyms, but I'll call out important bits.
[00:40] [00:40] Speaker 4: (screen share noise)
[00:45] Liam: Ok, so first slide: high level flow — step 1: embeddings via hosted embeddings endpoint, step 2: store vectors in your store (we don't force a vector DB), step 3: retrieve top-K, step 4: call hosted reranker with candidate docs + query, step 5: return ranked results. This lets you do dense-retrieval + neural rerank hosted in Redwood.
[01:10] Erin: When you say "hosted reranker" is that executed inside our VPC or on Redwood infra?
[01:15] Liam: Good question. The hosted public API runs on Redwood-managed infra. For AstraNova we discussed VPC/private deployment earlier — you have two options: Hosted (fast onboarding) or Private/VPC where the inference runs in your VPC with our control plane. For the pilot we usually start with hosted and then move to VPC if required.
[01:38] Ravi (AstraNova): For us security is primary. Is there a way to have the embeddings never leave our network? We were thinking of on-prem embeddings but still use Redwood reranker.
[01:45] Priya (Redwood): There's a hybrid approach — you can host embeddings generation in your VPC or on on-prem using Redwood Private, and then call reranker either in VPC or use a model that runs in Redwood hosted. But note that crossing networks introduces egress and latency. Also if you need end-to-end data residency the Private deployment is the better long-term choice.
[02:05] Daniel: Ok, what's the typical token latency for reranker? we care about interactive searches — sub 200ms is ideal but we know rerankers can be heavier.
[02:12] Liam: For small candidate sets (K=10) our optimized reranker on a p4-like SKU is usually in the 80–200ms range tail depending on sequence length. On hosted we observe median ~95ms in our bench, p95 ~220ms in heavy loads. For dedicated or private with pinned GPUs you can get lower and more predictable tails.
[02:35] Erin: That aligns with our expectations. And cost — are we billed per token for reranker as well?
[02:40] Maya: For hosted API, embeddings are billed per vector unit and rerank is per-token for the reranker call plus a small fixed per-request. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet but for pilot we usually give a small hosted credit.
[02:55] [03:00] Speaker 2: (brief cross talk)
[03:05] Liam: Now I'll demo a quick run. I'm going to use the hosted embeddings endpoint with a sample clinical note. I'll paste the curl call.
[03:12] Liam: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"rw-embed-compact-1","input":"Patient reports shortness of breath after exertion..."}'
[03:25] Liam: The response returns a 1536-d vector. Then we store that vector in your vector DB—example uses OpenSearch cluster for this demo.
[03:33] Erin: Oh we use milvus internally for dev, but OpenSearch is fine for demo.
[03:36] Liam: Great. Next step: retrieval returns top 25 candidates by cos sim, we then call hosted reranker like: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"model":"rw-rank-med-1","query":"shortness of breath after exertion","candidates":[{"id":"doc_123","text":"..."}, ...] }'
[03:56] Liam: The reranker takes the candidates and returns a score and optional span highlights.
[04:02] Nina (AstraNova): Are the spans hallucinated or do they reference exact doc offsets?
[04:06] Liam: They map back to document offsets when available, but small tokenization mismatches can occur — sometimes the transcript will show "K-V cache" as "K V cash" in text, little noisy tokens. We're working on making offsets more robust.
[04:20] Daniel: If we want to keep everything inside our VPC, which endpoints do we need to replicate? embeddings + reranker?
[04:25] Priya: For a fully private setup you'd run both embeddings and reranker inside the VPC, yes. You can mix: run embeddings in VPC and call Redwood's hosted reranker over secure peered link, but check your compliance team for egress.
[04:40] Ravi: On encryption — KMS support? we need envelope encryption with our HSM.
[04:45] Liam: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations) for Private deployments and dedicated. For hosted there's BYOK options in certain enterprise tiers; we can share the KMS integration doc.
[04:58] Maya: I'll ping that after the call.
[05:00] [05:00] Speaker 1: (typing sounds)
[05:05] Erik (typo in transcript: Speaker named Erik) — actually Erin: question about eval metrics — we track MRR and NDCG?
[05:10] Erin: yes, we want to compare to our current BM25 baseline across clinical query sets.
[05:14] Liam: Great. For pilot we suggest NDCG@10, MRR@10, and also latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) plus cost per query. We'll share a benchmark worksheet you can plug your ground truth into.
[05:28] Erin: Awesome. Can the reranker also accept structured metadata (e.g., encounter date, provider specialty) to bias results?
[05:34] Liam: Yes — you can pass structured fields as part of the candidate JSON, and the reranker can incorporate them. There's also a feature-called "score-fusion" that combines retrieval score, metadata boosts, and reranker score. The name in the UI is Redwood Optimize but sometimes transcribed as "Red wood optimize" in older notes.
[05:52] Daniel: For the pilot, how much infra do you need on our side? we can start minimal.
[05:56] Maya: Minimal: a vector store (can be managed or self-hosted), and ability to run a small data-transfer to Redwood test bucket if hosted. If you want VPC pilot, we'll need a peering/VPN and a small VM/GPU for private inference. We usually size pilot to a single GPU for rerank workloads.
[06:12] Erin: If we start with hosted, are there retention guarantees? we need 30-day data retention and searchable logs for audits.
[06:18] Priya: Hosted has configurable retention and audit logs. For regulated workloads we recommend Private so you control retention. We can set retention policies and export audit logs on request.
[06:28] Ravi: Any SOC2/ISO attestation?
[06:31] Liam: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified and has ISO 27001 in process; I'll share the certs and the compliance pack.
[06:38] [06:38] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[06:40] Liam: Switching to the console — demo time. I'm logging into Redwood Console, showing the model catalog. We have rw-embed-compact-1 and larger rw-embed-thera-2 (these model names sometimes get munged in transcript). You can pin model versions and see per-model performance metrics, token costs, and backlog.
[06:58] Liam: Here is the rerank job in the console — you can run an on-demand rerank with our test harness and see scoring breakdown: lexical vs semantic vs metadata.
[07:08] Erin: Can we run batch re-ranking jobs for nightly re-ranks?
[07:12] Liam: Yes, both on-demand and scheduled re-ranks. Batch jobs are cheaper because we can batch across queries and use autoscaling.
[07:20] Daniel: Do you do automatic caching of KV caches across runs? we have long documents and are worried about warm-up costs.
[07:26] Liam: The runtime manages KV caching for decoder-style models; for rerankers (encoder-only) caching is less relevant. For generative flows we do prefix caching, yes. For rerankers we focus on batching and multi-query optimization. There's also a suggestion engine in Redwood Optimize to tune batch sizes/caching thresholds.
[07:45] Nina: For medical records we also want deterministic outputs for audit trails — can we freeze model versions and have deterministic seeds?
[07:51] Priya: You can pin model versions and disable non-deterministic sampling. For reranking deterministic ranking is default unless you request sampling.
[07:58] Erin: About quantization — does the reranker support int8 or lower precision for cost savings?
[08:03] Liam: Defensive answer: yes, we support quantized model variants in Dedicated/Private deployments; in hosted we have quantized variants for some models. Quantization can change numeric behavior slightly so we recommend running evals to detect regressions. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
[08:18] Daniel: Let's talk scale — if we go beyond pilot to 2M queries/month, how does routing work?
[08:24] Liam: Smart routing: requests can be routed by policy — latency-first to more powerful pools, cost-first to cheaper quantized variants. You can do fallbacks if a pool is saturated. For large scale we recommend Dedicated to guarantee throughput.
[08:36] [08:36] Speaker 2: (background noise)
[08:40] Maya: Time check — we have about 20 minutes left. We'll run a quick live example end-to-end against a sanitized subset of your data. Erin, you shared a small sample earlier?
[08:49] Erin: I uploaded a 200-document sanitized sample to the shared bucket this morning.
[08:52] Liam: Perfect. I'm switching to the notebook. I'll run a quick retrieval+rerank and show the console performance panel.
[09:05] [09:05] (pen clicking)
[09:08] Liam: Running retrieval... top candidates returned in 120ms — then reranker call in 110ms. The console shows combined latency ~230ms for this end-to-end, which is acceptable for interactive UI. Caveat: this is small scale.
[09:24] Daniel: That's decent. What about cost per query ballpark?
[09:27] Maya: For the model variants used in this demo, ballpark is $0.0009–$0.002 per query depending on candidate size and model, but we'll provide a detailed per-query cost sheet.
[09:40] Erin: Can we A/B test reranker variants in production?
[09:43] Priya: Yes — console supports canary rollouts and A/B testing. You can run two reranker models and compare NDCG on live traffic and have automated rollback if quality drops.
[09:55] Ravi: For audit we need request-level trace logs; do you expose trace IDs?
[09:59] Liam: Yes, we emit trace IDs and per-request latency/cost breakdown. You can forward logs to your SIEM.
[10:06] [10:06] Speaker 4: (muffled)
[10:10] Erin: One more question — does Redwood have an embeddings-only hosted option where we host embeddings and don't touch content?
[10:16] Liam: Hosted embeddings will see content unless you use a Private embeddings deployment. You could also use self-hosted embeddings and only send vectors to Redwood, but note vectors can leak semantics; if you need no data to leave your network, keep everything in VPC.
[10:30] Maya: Ok, let's go to the pilot checklist slide. Key items: dataset upload, evaluation queries & ground truth, security review (SOC2 docs + KMS), pilot contract + pilot SLOs.
[10:45] Daniel: Timeline — we'd like a pilot next week, 2–3 weeks long. Is that feasible?
[10:50] Maya: Yes, feasible. Pilot kickoff early next week pending paperwork. We'll provision a small test key and credit.
[10:58] Erin: For the pilot success criteria we propose: NDCG improvement over BM25 by 15% and median query latency <250ms.
[11:06] Priya: Sounds reasonable; we'll include that in the proposal as measurable goals.
[11:12] [11:12] Speaker 2: (cough)
[11:15] Liam: Quick note on integrability — sample SDKs in Python/JS. Example snippet: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=...); emb = c.embeddings.create(model='rw-embed-compact-1', input='...') — this is in our quickstart.
[11:30] Nina: We use Go primarily — is there a Go SDK?
[11:33] Maya: Yes, we have community Go SDK + internal examples. We'll send code snippets.
[11:38] Daniel: Ok can you also include a recommended schema for storing vectors and metadata in our Milvus cluster?
[11:43] Liam: We'll send a Milvus schema example with recommended shard sizes and replica counts for pilot.
[11:50] [11:50] (short silence)
[11:54] Maya: Any last questions?
[11:56] Ravi: Only one — if we hit a regression in relevance after upgrading model versions, what's the rollback procedure?
[12:02] Priya: You can pin to previous model, console supports automated rollbacks and A/B. Also, Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts against a prompt set and trigger rollbacks.
[12:12] Daniel: Great. Thanks everyone.
[12:15] Maya: Thanks — recap of next steps: Maya to send pilot proposal + pricing; Liam to share VPC/KMS/compliance docs and Milvus schema; Erin to upload full 1k doc eval set; schedule 2-hr kickoff next Tues.
[12:30] Erin: Sounds good.
[12:32] Daniel: We'll review and get back with legal/security questions.
[12:35] Maya: Perfect. I'll follow up with calendar invite and links. Thanks all.
[12:40] (meeting end)
